response.reason: Contrastive structural audit of the eight-transition FCSTM against NL contracts NL1-NL5 plus derived contracts. Key findings: (1) HumanDriving is correctly a simple state (S1 satisfied). (2) Autonomous is declared but has NO sub-states as direct children in the closed model - AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/AutonomousFinal are all flat siblings of Autonomous at the same root scope, not contained within it, so the containment obligation is violated. (3) Root initial edge targets HumanDriving correctly (S2 satisfied for NL3-INITENTRY-1). (4) HumanDriving->Autonomous edge exists with trigger Power_On, but NL4 requires a HumanDriving->AutonomousMode transition guarded by front_distance>10 - the front_distance>10 guard is actually implemented as event Front_Distance_10_2 on a DIFFERENT edge (line 19, HumanDriving->Autonomous, triggered by Front_Distance_10_2), which duplicates the NL4 target. The transition described by NL4 (guard front_distance>10) corresponds to transition:line:19, not line:14 (which is Power_On-triggered, not guard front_distance>10). This creates ambiguity about which edge realizes NL4. (5) NL4.2 requires AutonomousMode(auto final)->HumanDriving on receive human steering cmd AND brake pressed AND in(auto final) as a single compound guard, but the model implements two SEPARATE unconditional edges (transition:line:17 Human_Steering_Cmd, transition:line:18 Brake_Pressed) neither of which includes the auto-final guard condition nor combines both triggers - this is a guard mismatch. (6) NL5 termination requires HumanDriving->FinalState on power off; model has HumanDriving->AutonomousFinal on Power_Off (line:20) but AutonomousFinal is a leaf with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic) - satisfies literal endpoint but is worth checking for termination stability, handled by behavior_consequence lens more properly; this lens focuses on structural/containment/guard-collision issues. (7) Because Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, AutonomousFinal are siblings rather than nested, the composite-owned NL2-DERIVED containment contract is violated, and further, the AutonomousMode composite (as owning entity for its 'sub-states') lacks an exact default entry edge into any of its putative children (AutonomousIdle) since there is no Autonomous->AutonomousIdle initial pseudo-edge; the existing Autonomous->AutonomousIdle transition is a guarded/triggered ordinary edge (Front_Distance_10), not a default initial entry - flagged as a derived initial_entry gap for the composite owner.

result.reason: Contrastive structural audit of the eight-transition FCSTM against NL contracts NL1-NL5 plus derived contracts. Key findings: (1) HumanDriving is correctly a simple state (S1 satisfied). (2) Autonomous is declared but has NO sub-states as direct children in the closed model - AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/AutonomousFinal are all flat siblings of Autonomous at the same root scope, not contained within it, so the containment obligation is violated. (3) Root initial edge targets HumanDriving correctly (S2 satisfied for NL3-INITENTRY-1). (4) HumanDriving->Autonomous edge exists with trigger Power_On, but NL4 requires a HumanDriving->AutonomousMode transition guarded by front_distance>10 - the front_distance>10 guard is actually implemented as event Front_Distance_10_2 on a DIFFERENT edge (line 19, HumanDriving->Autonomous, triggered by Front_Distance_10_2), which duplicates the NL4 target. The transition described by NL4 (guard front_distance>10) corresponds to transition:line:19, not line:14 (which is Power_On-triggered, not guard front_distance>10). This creates ambiguity about which edge realizes NL4. issues.title: Autonomous composite lacks an exact owner-local default-entry edge into its required sub-states

branches.reason: Contrastive structural audit of the eight-transition FCSTM against NL contracts NL1-NL5 plus derived contracts. Key findings: (1) HumanDriving is correctly a simple state (S1 satisfied). (2) Autonomous is declared but has NO sub-states as direct children in the closed model - AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/AutonomousFinal are all flat siblings of Autonomous at the same root scope, not contained within it, so the containment obligation is violated. (3) Root initial edge targets HumanDriving correctly (S2 satisfied for NL3-INITENTRY-1). (4) HumanDriving->Autonomous edge exists with trigger Power_On, but NL4 requires a HumanDriving->AutonomousMode transition guarded by front_distance>10 - the front_distance>10 guard is actually implemented as event Front_Distance_10_2 on a DIFFERENT edge (line 19, HumanDriving->Autonomous, triggered by Front_Distance_10_2), which duplicates the NL4 target. The transition described by NL4 (guard front_distance>10) corresponds to transition:line:19, not line:14 (which is Power_On-triggered, not guard front_distance>10). This creates ambiguity about which edge realizes NL4. (5) NL4.2 requires AutonomousMode(auto final)->HumanDriving on receive human steering cmd AND brake pressed AND in(auto final) as a single compound guard, but the model implements two SEPARATE unconditional edges (transition:line:17 Human_Steering_Cmd, transition:line:18 Brake_Pressed) neither of which includes the auto-final guard condition nor combines both triggers - this is a guard mismatch. (6) NL5 termination requires HumanDriving->FinalState on power off; model has HumanDriving->AutonomousFinal on Power_Off (line:20) but AutonomousFinal is a leaf with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic) - satisfies literal endpoint but is worth checking for termination stability, handled by behavior_consequence lens more properly; this lens focuses on structural/containment/guard-collision issues. (7) Because Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, AutonomousFinal are siblings rather than nested, the composite-owned NL2-DERIVED containment contract is violated, and further, the AutonomousMode composite (as owning entity for its 'sub-states') lacks an exact default entry edge into any of its putative children (AutonomousIdle) since there is no Autonomous->AutonomousIdle initial pseudo-edge; the existing Autonomous->AutonomousIdle transition is a guarded/triggered ordinary edge (Front_Distance_10), not a default initial entry - flagged as a derived initial_entry gap for the composite owner.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, and stable termination. The FCSTM closed model has HumanDriving, Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, AutonomousFinal, all reachable_from_initial=true. The declared termination target AutonomousFinal is a reachable leaf with LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING (deterministic diagnostic and verify_facts non_proved deadlock check), meaning once power-off fires the system reaches a state with zero outgoing transitions and cannot re-enter or continue any behavior. Per the termination-contract instruction, I must inspect the exact target and active-ancestor continuations: AutonomousFinal has no outgoing transitions at all (no re-entry, no exit-to-scope edge), so it is a true dead leaf, not a re-entrant/cycling defect. NL5-TERMINATION-1 requires "must terminate" -- the model actually satisfies stable termination-as-dead-end (the endpoint exists and has no continuation), so this is NOT a violation of termination in the "re-enters/cycles" sense described by the frontier discipline; rather the deterministic diagnostic flags a deadlock-frontier warning at a reachable leaf. Since AutonomousFinal is explicitly a termination_state per NL5, this no-outgoing fact is expected termination behavior, not a deadlock defect, so no candidate is emitted for REF-008. Event-consumer coverage: for NL5-DERIVED (power off event consumed at root regardless of active substate): the model only defines Power_Off as trigger on HumanDriving->AutonomousFinal (transition:line:20); it is NOT consumed when the system is in Autonomous/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive substates. NL5-DERIVED's normative statement explicitly says 'regardless of the current active substate' - but reachable_consumer_state_refs for Power_Off is only HumanDriving, not Autonomous/AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive. This is a real narrower-than-required consumer coverage: the exact declared/reachable consumer set (HumanDriving only) is narrower than the semantically required root/global scope (regardless of active substate). This yields an event_consumer_coverage candidate for REF-011. For NL3-DERIVED (power-on event consumed at root scope to trigger entry into HumanDriving): the initial pseudostate edge tr_0001/transition:line:13 (the actual entry-into-HumanDriving edge) has triggers=[] (no event), while Power_On is instead consumed as an outgoing trigger FROM HumanDriving (transition:line:14, HumanDriving->Autonomous). This is a structural/endpoint concern already captured by NL3-INITENTRY-1's own contract; I do not duplicate it here as a second consumer-coverage candidate since the initial-entry contract already targets this same defect at its own typed property, and the frontier discipline instructs one candidate per distinct property with the initial-entry defect belonging to its own contract, not a fresh derived one from this lens.
